input: Plan a neighborhood skill-sharing swap event

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of participants and range of skills included determines the complexity of logistics, scheduling, and space needed.
Knowing whether this is organized by one person, a small committee, or an existing community group shapes how responsibilities are divided and what resources are already available.
The venue (outdoor, community center, someone's home) and timing affect permits, layout, capacity, and accessibility planning.
A defined budget determines whether printed materials, catering, equipment rentals, or paid promotion are realistic options.
The format of the swap — e.g., open fair style, scheduled one-on-one sessions, or rotating stations — fundamentally changes how the event is structured and run.
The desired tone (casual block-party feel vs. structured workshop series) shapes communication style, signage, facilitation, and overall participant experience.
Understanding what a successful outcome looks like — strong turnout, meaningful connections, repeat attendance — determines what to measure and prioritize during planning.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a neighborhood skill-sharing swap event
gold.taskDescription: Organize a community event where neighbors exchange skills, knowledge, or services with one another.

questions.title: How many neighbors do you expect to participate?
questions.description: Understanding the anticipated headcount helps determine venue size, number of skill slots, and overall logistical complexity.

questions.title: Are you organizing this alone or with a group?
questions.description: Clarifying who is involved in planning reveals what roles need to be assigned and what resources or networks are already in place.

questions.title: Do you have a venue and date already in mind?
questions.description: Knowing the location type and timing affects permits, layout, weather contingencies, and scheduling decisions.

questions.title: What is your budget for this event?
questions.description: A clear budget sets boundaries on printed materials, refreshments, equipment, and outreach methods.

questions.title: What format do you want the skill swap to take?
questions.description: Choosing between an open fair, rotating stations, or scheduled one-on-one sessions determines the entire structural design of the event.

questions.title: Should this feel casual and social or structured and workshop-like?
questions.description: The desired tone shapes how the event is promoted, facilitated, and experienced by attendees.

questions.title: What would make this event a clear success for you?
questions.description: Defining success criteria — such as turnout numbers, new connections formed, or plans for a follow-up event — guides prioritization throughout the planning process.
